nl.statement: A single trajectory \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) from a time-homogeneous partially observed Markov decision process on a finite joint state space \(\mathcal S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal H\) with binary action alphabet \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) and rewards bounded by one in absolute value. The primitives are a joint reward-transition kernel \(K(dy,dx',dh'\mid x,h,a)\), a known memoryless behavior policy \(b\) and a known memoryless target policy \(e\); derived from them are the policy-induced joint-state kernels \(P_p\), their stationary laws \(d_p\), the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\), the stationary target value \(\theta(K,e)\), and the observable one-step policy ratio \(\rho_t\). The regime parameters are the mixing scale \(t_0\), the log policy-overlap bound \(\zeta\) and the latent stationary-overlap radius \(C\), with derived constants \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\) and \(L=e^{\zeta}\). The latent coordinates \(H_t\), the joint states \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\) and both stationary laws are unobserved; only \(\mathsf O_T\) — the observed states \(X_t\), the actions \(A_t\) and the reward VALUES \(Y_t\in[-1,1]\) — together with \(b\), \(e\) and the observed alphabet is revealed. A trajectory of length \(T\) consists of the joint states \(S_1,\ldots,S_{T+1}\) together with the action-reward pairs \((A_t,Y_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\): at each epoch \(t\) the action is drawn from \(b(\cdot\mid X_t)\) and the kernel \(K\) generates the pair \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) from \((S_t,A_t)\), so the terminal state \(S_{T+1}\) belongs to the trajectory while the observation records only the first \(T\) states, and of those only their observed coordinates. An estimator sees each epoch exactly through the triple \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\): its argument is the sequence of those triples itself, and the reward enters only through its real value in \([-1,1]\). No restriction is placed on the reward law beyond that bound: the conditional law of \(Y_t\) under \(K\) may be any probability law on \([-1,1]\), discrete, continuous or mixed. — Current P15 architecture. `JointState nX nH := Fin nX × Fin nH`. `Step nX nH := ℝ × JointState nX nH`. `FullTrajectory T nX nH := (Fin (T + 1) → JointState nX nH) × (Fin T → Bool × ℝ)`. `ObsView T nX := Fin T → (Fin nX × Bool × ℝ)` is the projection to `(X_t, A_t, Y_t)` from the first T states and the T action/reward coordinates; the terminal state is not observed. `K : JointState nX nH → Bool → Measure (ℝ × JointState nX nH)` has an arbitrary real reward law supported on `[-1,1]`. There is no class-level reward alphabet or coding map.

The observable-data decision problem attached to \(\mathrm S_1\). The cardinality-uniform experiment class \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) collects all such trajectory experiments, over unrestricted finite observed and latent alphabets, satisfying the seven class predicates. An estimator is any measurable function of \(\mathsf O_T\) — whose entries are the observed states, actions and reward values \(Y_t\in[-1,1]\) — together with \(b\), \(e\), \(t_0\), \(\zeta\), \(C\) and the observed alphabet, and the risk is squared error against \(\theta(K,e)\); \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the infimum over estimators of the supremum over the class, with comparison constants \(c_\star\le c^\star\) and threshold \(T_\star\). Because \(\theta(K,e)\in[-1,1]\), projecting an estimator onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase its squared error at any model, so every measurable estimator is dominated pointwise by a \([-1,1]\)-valued one; consequently the infimum over the \([-1,1]\)-valued estimators is at most the worst-case risk of any measurable estimator, and every lower bound proved against the restricted family holds pointwise against every measurable estimator. The competing family is taken to consist of the measurable \([-1,1]\)-valued functions of the trajectory of triples \(((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^{T}\) itself, together with \(b\), \(e\) and the regime parameters; this restricts the problem in no way that matters, because the candidate estimators below are of this form by construction, and each converse below is established pointwise against every measurable function of the trajectory whose mean squared error is finite at the two comparison models — an estimator with infinite mean squared error at one of them violates no risk lower bound. The candidate estimators are the clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimators \(\widehat\theta_k\) built from the scores \(Z_t(k)=Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j\), run at the balanced depth \(k_T\) or at the radius-adaptive depth \(\kappa_T^{\mathrm{rad}}(C)\). The rate parameters are the exponent \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), the normalized overlap radius \(q_C=(C-1)/C\), the shrinking overlap excess \(\delta_T\) defining the local radius \(C_T=1+\delta_T\), and the local-overlap derivation handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{loc}}\). — Current P15 decision architecture. `ModelIndex T t0 zeta C` carries only `nX`, `nH`, the raw experiment, and class membership. `RawEstimator T := (nX : Nat) → Policy nX → Policy nX → ObsView T nX → ℝ`. `ObservableEstimator T` is the subtype of such estimators that are measurable and `[-1,1]`-valued. Estimators receive only `nX`, revealed `b`, revealed `e`, and `ObsView`; they receive no reward-alphabet or coding data, latent-state data, kernel, stationary law, or terminal state. The regime parameters are closed over by `minimaxRisk`.

The signed-depth two-point sub-experiment inside \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for \(C>1\). The observed state is constant, the hidden state is \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\) with depth \(J_t\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\) and sign \(U_t\in\{-1,+1\}\), the behavior policy plays action one with probability \(1/L\) and the target policy plays action one surely. A reset draws the sign with bias \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\); an advance retains the sign under action one and refreshes it under action zero; at terminal depth the reward is Rademacher with mean \(vc_0U_t\), where \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\) and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\) indexes the two alternatives. The depth marginal is stationary with masses \(w_j=(1-\alpha)\alpha^j/(1-\alpha^{Q+1})\), and the two induced observed-path laws are \(\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\). Attached to them is the observed filtration \(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sigma(A_1,Y_1,\ldots,A_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\), with observed prefix length \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), predictive terminal posterior \(q_t^v=\Pr_v(J_t=Q\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\), rare-action-history factor \(a_t^{(Q)}\), and the two constants \(B_0\) (observed divergence) and \(K_0\) (uniform terminal posterior). — PROCESS. ROUND-9 FRAMING (decision P14 part (5)), which is what keeps this whole block intact: the signed-depth family is built as a `FiniteRewardModel T 1 (2*(Q+1)) 2` and then `embed`ed into the real-reward class of S1, so every computation described below stays a FINITE computation and only the final KL budget and the absolute-continuity discharge are transported to the real-reward observed law -- by `InformationTheory.klDiv_map_le` (data processing, the `<=` direction the converse needs) and `MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.map` respectively, through the Helpers/FiniteEncoding.lean bridges `embed_klDiv_le` and `embed_absolutelyContinuous`. The witness is a genuine member of the real-reward class (its rewards are Rademacher, a bounded real law that happens to be finitely supported), so nothing about the converse is weakened by the world change; what WAS weakened before round 9 was the upper bracket, which is a claim over the whole class and is repaired in S1/S2. Lean carrier (at the FiniteRewardModel level): latent alphabet Fin (Q+1) x Bool encoded as Fin (2*(Q+1)); observed alphabet Fin 1; reward alphabet Fin 2 with rew = ![-1,1] (injective, which is why conditioning on the symbol prefix and on the real reward prefix generate the same information and the filter realization below is faithful for the embedded law). `\(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\)` is realized as conditioning on the observed prefix `Fin t -> (Bool x Fin 2)` (a Fintype), so `q_t^v` and `a_t^{(Q)}` are ordinary real-valued functions of a prefix rather than sigma-algebra objects -- the standard finite-alphabet realization of a filtration, and the only encoding that keeps the chain-rule step elementary. REUSE for the divergence step: the observed-path KL is factored with Mathlib's `InformationTheory.klDiv_compProd_eq_add` (Mathlib/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/ChainRule.lean, the full chain rule KL(mu (x) kappa, nu (x) eta) = KL(mu,nu) + integral of KL(kappa,eta)) and `InformationTheory.klDiv_compProd_left`; the action conditionals cancel through `Causalean.Mathlib.InformationTheory.Measure.klDiv_compProd_left`. The testing floor is `Causalean.Stat.bretagnolle_huber_affinity` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/BretagnolleHuber.lean:373), used DIRECTLY: it states `(1/2) * Real.exp (-(klDiv mu nu).toReal) <= 1 - tvDist mu nu`, which is verbatim the note's (24) overlap inequality with an EXPLICIT constant, and it composes with `Causalean.Stat.real_two_point_lower_bound` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean:61, the note's sign-classification step) and Mathlib's `mul_meas_ge_le_integral_of_nonneg` (the note's (25) squared-loss event bound) to give the explicit two-point floor. So the note's 'Jensen + Cauchy-Schwarz + sign classification' paragraph is REPLACED by reuse and does not need reproving, but the composition is done in the paper-local primitive `two_point_floor_explicit` (Helpers/TwoPoint.lean) rather than by calling `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.le_cam_two_point_mse`. ROUND-3 CORRECTION (decision P8): the earlier version of this note claimed le_cam_two_point_mse 'already packages exp(-K)/32 as the constant' -- that is FALSE at the level of its statement, which concludes only `exists cK, 0 < cK and ..`; the witness exp(-K)/32 is picked inside its proof (LeCamTwoPoint.lean:239) and is invisible to consumers. That reuse therefore stays available for the EXISTENTIAL-rate converses only, and the explicit-constant floors go through the three public ingredients just named. ROUND-4 CORRECTION (decision P9): `bretagnolle_huber_affinity` states its floor as `(1/2) * Real.exp (-(klDiv mu nu).toReal) <= 1 - tvDist mu nu`, so converting a budget written as `klDiv <= ENNReal.ofReal K` into the displayed `Real.exp (-K)` needs `(klDiv).toReal <= K`, i.e. `ENNReal.toReal_mono` plus `ENNReal.toReal_ofReal`, and the latter REQUIRES `0 <= K` (for K < 0 the step is false, not merely unproved). The primitive `two_point_floor_explicit` therefore carries an explicit `(hK : 0 <= K)` premise, threaded through both tiers and through every consumer; it is discharged by `norm_num` at the two concrete budgets this world supplies, K = 1/4 (the equal-policy Rademacher pair, writeup.tex eq. (32)/(10)) and K = 1/8 (the signed-depth pair, writeup.tex eqs. (23)/(14)/(34)). ROUND-5 CORRECTION (decision P10): `bretagnolle_huber_affinity` also requires `hac : mu << nu` and `hfin : klDiv mu nu <> top`, and these are NOT free on this world's Fintype observed-path space -- finiteness of `FiniteObsView T 1 2` gives measurability and llr-integrability (`MeasureTheory.Integrable.of_finite`) but says nothing about which observed words carry mass, and a degenerate in-class member can charge a word its partner does not. What actually discharges them here is the STRICT POSITIVITY this world does have, and the writeup already proves: b(1) = 1/L in (0,1) so both actions have positive behaviour probability, and every conditional reward probability lies in [(1 - c_0)/2, (1 + c_0)/2] with c_0 = (1 - alpha)/4 in (0, 1/4), so every observed word has positive mass. That sentence becomes the lemma `signedDepth_fullSupportObs : FullSupportObs (signedDepthFamily ..)` in Helpers/SignedDepth.lean, fed to the generic bridges `obsLaw_absolutelyContinuous_of_fullSupport` and `klDiv_ne_top_of_fullSupport` (Helpers/Kernels.lean, over `PMF.toMeasure_apply_singleton` and `InformationTheory.klDiv_ne_top_iff`). The same lemma is what makes this world's KL BUDGET meaningful at all: without it `klDiv` is `top` and the budget inequality is false, so the support work is load-bearing regardless of whether F2 keeps `hac`/`hfin` as premises or re-derives them from the budget the way LeCamTwoPoint.lean:266-269 does. No other part of this block changes: the chain-rule reuse, the filter realization and the two-point composition are exactly as at round 3. A refreshed finite-state insulin-policy adaptation \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\): a \(360\)-state controlled Markov model whose state \(s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) records a discretized glucose level, two lagged diet indicators, two lagged activity levels and the previous action. The diet coordinates form the latent state \(H_t\) and all remaining coordinates form the observed state \(X_t\); the behavior policy injects insulin with probability \(3/10\) and the target policy injects exactly when glucose is at least \(125\). With probability one half the next full state is uniform, and otherwise the next glucose is a Gaussian autoregressive update rounded to the grid while the memories shift. The reward is a deterministic four-valued function of glucose. The diagnostic \(\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}\) is the difference between the stationary expectation of \(Y_te(A_t\mid X_t)/b(A_t\mid X_t)\) and \(\theta(K,e)\) in this model. — PROCESS. The earlier entry mis-set `disposition:"reuse"` with `reuse: ...RatInterval`, which named a certificate-layer numeric helper as if it were the ambient world -- RatInterval binds neither `\(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\)` nor `\(\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}\)` and cannot, since it is a rational-interval type with no experiment, policy, kernel or stationary law in it. The finite data are unchanged (observed alphabet 5 glucose x 3 x 3 activity x 2 previous action = 90, latent diet alphabet {0,78}^2 = 4, reward alphabet {-1,-2/3,-1/3,0} of size 4, kernel = (1/2) uniform refresh + (1/2) action-specific Gaussian-rounded update at the cut points 75/125/175/225, b(1|x) = 3/10, e(1|x) = indicator g >= 125), and `noncomputable def immediateWeightBias (T : Nat) : R` realising \(\Delta_{\mathrm{imm}}\) as the stationary expectation of Y_t * ratio b e X_t A_t minus `targetValue (insulinGrid T)` -- i.e. both are instances of the S1 world's own `RawPomdpExperiment` / `policyKernel` / `stationaryLaw` / `targetValue` machinery, which is why this block only NARROWS S1 and adds no new abstraction. Identify the numeric action alphabet \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) with the Boolean action set by \(0\leftrightarrow \mathrm{false}\) and \(1\leftrightarrow \mathrm{true}\). The behavior carrier \(b\) is a probability vector at each observed state,
\[
b(a\mid x)\ge 0
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X,\ a\in\mathcal A,
\qquad
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A} b(a\mid x)=1
\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
For every \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\), the joint law of the state-and-epoch history strictly before \(t\), the current joint state \((X_t,H_t)\), and the current action \(A_t\) factors as the law of that history and current joint state followed by the behavior kernel evaluated at the current observed state:
\[
\mathbb P\!\left\{
\bigl((X_s,H_s)_{s<t},(A_s,Y_s)_{s<t},(X_t,H_t),A_t\bigr)\in dh\,da
\right\}
=
\mathbb P\!\left\{
\bigl((X_s,H_s)_{s<t},(A_s,Y_s)_{s<t},(X_t,H_t)\bigr)\in dh
\right\}
\, b(da\mid X_t(h)).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\),
\[
\Pr\!\left(A_t=a\mid X_{0:t},H_{0:t},A_{0:t-1},Y_{0:t-1}\right)
=
b(a\mid X_t).
\]

review.note: The factorization conditions on exactly the past states, actions, rewards, and current state stated in the paper and assigns the current action through b at the current observed state; PolicyVector merely exposes the declared policy codomain.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C):=\{(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)): T\in\mathbb N,\ |\mathcal X|<\infty,\ |\mathcal H|<\infty,\ |\mathcal A|=2,\text{ and }\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{ign}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{start}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{reward}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{act}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{mix}},\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{stat}}\text{ hold}\}\), where the seven predicates are exactly \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\) through \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}stationary\text{-}overlap}\); the union ranges over all finite cardinalities and all revealed policy pairs.
nl.frozen_body:
For \(T\in\mathbb N\) and \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the class of all observable-data POMDP experiments
\[
(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))
\]
with the following defining properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Horizon and alphabets.)} The trajectory horizon satisfies \(1\le T\), the observed and latent alphabets \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal H\) are finite, and \(|\mathcal A|=2\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter scales.)} The mixing and log-overlap parameters satisfy \(0<t_0\) and \(0<\zeta\).
\item \textbf{(Raw experiment.)} The tuple has a reward-transition kernel \(K\), behavior policy \(b\), target policy \(e\), and probability law \(\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)\) for the observed trajectory generated from the joint state coordinates \((X_t,H_t)\).
\item \textbf{(Seven restrictions.)} The seven restrictions in \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel,obj:ass:sequential-ignorability,obj:ass:stationary-start,obj:ass:bounded-reward,obj:ass:policy-overlap,obj:ass:uniform-contraction,obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap} hold, with policy-overlap factor \(L=\exp(\zeta)\) and contraction factor \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
:=
\left\{
(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)):
\begin{array}{l}
1\le T,\quad |\mathcal X|<\infty,\quad |\mathcal H|<\infty,\quad |\mathcal A|=2,\\
0<t_0,\quad 0<\zeta,\\
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{pomdp}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{reward}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{act}},
\mathrm A_{\mathrm{mix}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{stat}}\text{ hold}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class ranges over all finite observed and latent cardinalities and all revealed behavior-target policy pairs satisfying these conditions.

review.note: The indexed membership structure imposes exactly the seven paper predicates; Nat/Fin/Bool encode unrestricted finite alphabets and binary actions, while t0_pos and zeta_pos enforce the declared parameter domains.

nl.frozen_body:
For the joint state \(S_t\) and the target-policy reward regression \(g_e\),
\[
\theta(K,e)
:=
\sum_{s=(x,h)\in\mathcal S} d_e(s)g_e(s)
=
\sum_{s=(x,h)\in\mathcal S} d_e(s)
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
e(a\mid x)\,E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a].
\]

review.note: Unfolding rewardRegression gives exactly the target-policy action average of the K-row reward expectation, weighted over states by the selected target stationary law.

nl.statement: \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C):=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\sigma(\mathsf O_T,b,e,t_0,\zeta,C)}\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}E_M[(\widehat\theta-\theta(K,e))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable estimators and the supplied finite observed alphabets are included in the estimator's information.
nl.frozen_body:
For a trajectory horizon \(T\ge 1\) and parameters \(t_0,\zeta,C\), the cardinality-uniform observable-data minimax squared-error risk is
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\theta}
\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
\mathbb E_{\operatorname{Law}^{\mathrm{obs}}_M}
\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\theta(n_X,b,e,\mathsf O_T)-\theta(K,e)\right\}^2
\right].
\]
Here \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) is the finite observed- and latent-state model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with unrestricted finite observed alphabet size \(n_X\) and unrestricted finite latent alphabet size, and \(\theta(K,e)\) is the stationary target-policy mean reward in \cref{obj:def:target-value}. The positive-horizon requirement \(1\le T\) is part of membership in \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), not a separate restriction on the supremum; at the degenerate horizon \(T=0\) the class is empty and the display is not used. The infimum ranges over all observable-data estimators \(\widehat\theta\) that take as inputs only \(n_X\), \(b\), \(e\), and the observed trajectory view \(\mathsf O_T\), are measurable in \(\mathsf O_T\) for each \(n_X,b,e\), and are uniformly valued in \([-1,1]\).

review.note: Unfolding minimaxValue, observedRisk, and sqRisk gives infimum over measurable observable-data estimator families and supremum over the cardinality-uniform ModelIndex class; restricting estimators to [-1,1] preserves the infimum because model-class target values lie in [-1,1] and measurable clipping weakly decreases squared error.

nl.statement: For \(0\le k<T\), define \(\widehat\theta_k:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}\{(T-k)^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}Z_t(k)\}\), with \(Z_t(k)=Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j\) and the zero-cell convention in the definition of \(\rho_t\).
nl.frozen_body:
For \(0\le k<T\), define
\[
Z_t(k)
:=
Y_t\prod_{j=t-k}^{t}\rho_j,
\]
where \(\rho_t\) is the observable one-step policy ratio with the zero-cell convention. The clipped partial-history importance-weighted estimator is
\[
\widehat\theta_k
:=
\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
\left\{
\frac{1}{T-k}\sum_{t=k}^{T-1} Z_t(k)
\right\}.
\]

review.note: After unfolding clipUnit, phiwRaw, phiwScore, and ratio, Lean exactly implements the clipped average over paper epochs k+1 through T, including the chronological k+1-factor ratio product and zero-cell convention.

nl.frozen_body:
For the contraction parameter \(\alpha\) and policy-overlap constant \(L\), the balanced fixed-radius history depth is
\[
k_T
:=
\min\left\{
\left\lfloor\frac{T}{2}\right\rfloor,
\max\left\{
0,
\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(T)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}
\right\rfloor
\right\}
\right\}.
\]

review.note: Nat division realizes floor(T/2), Int.toNat realizes max(0,·), and unfolding mixingAlpha and policyFactor yields exactly alpha=exp(-1/t0) and L=exp(zeta).

nl.statement: For \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(X_t\) constant, \(H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}\), \(b(1)=1/L\), and \(e(1)=1\). Draw a reset sign from \(\Pr(U= u)=(1+u\varepsilon_C)/2\). If \(J_t=Q\), set \(J_{t+1}=0\) and draw a reset sign. If \(J_t<Q\), reset in the same way with probability \(1-\alpha\); otherwise set \(J_{t+1}=J_t+1\), retaining \(U_t\) when \(A_t=1\) and replacing it by an independent fair sign when \(A_t=0\). Independently of the next-state draw conditional on \((J_t,U_t,A_t)\), draw \(Y_t\in\{-1,+1\}\) with \(\Pr_v(Y_t=y\mid J_t,U_t,A_t)=\{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1(J_t=Q)\}/2\). Initialize from the behavior-stationary law \(d_b(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j})/2\).

For a trajectory length \(T\), parameters \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), a terminal depth \(Q\in\mathbb N\), and an alternative index \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth family is defined under
\[
t_0>0,\qquad \zeta>0,\qquad C>1,\qquad Q\ge 1.
\]
It is the raw POMDP experiment in \(\mathsf O_T\) with one observed state and \(2(Q+1)\) hidden states obtained by embedding the following finite-reward model.  The observed coordinate \(X_t\) is constant, and the hidden coordinate is written
\[
H_t=(J_t,U_t)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\times\{-1,+1\}.
\]
Writing \(\alpha\) for the mixing value determined by \(t_0\), \(L\) for the policy factor determined by \(\zeta\), \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\), and \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), the behavior and target policies are
\[
b(A_t=1)=\frac{1}{L},\qquad b(A_t=0)=1-\frac{1}{L},
\qquad
e(A_t=1)=1,\qquad e(A_t=0)=0.
\]
The initial hidden-state law is the probability measure obtained from the weights
\[
w_j\frac{1+u\varepsilon_C L^{-j}}{2},
\qquad
w_j=
\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^j}{1-\alpha^{Q+1}},
\qquad
j\in\{0,\ldots,Q\},\ u\in\{-1,+1\}.
\]
The transition kernel is the probability measure on reward-symbol and next-hidden-state pairs whose real weight at \((y,H_{t+1})\), with \(y\in\{-1,+1\}\), is the product of the reward weight
\[
\frac{1+yvc_0U_t\mathbf 1\{J_t=Q\}}{2}
\]
and the hidden-transition weight specified as follows.  A reset sign \(u'\) has weight
\[
\frac{1+u'\varepsilon_C}{2}.
\]
If \(J_t=Q\), then only transitions with \(J_{t+1}=0\) receive this reset-sign weight.  If \(J_t<Q\), transitions with \(J_{t+1}=0\) receive weight \((1-\alpha)(1+U_{t+1}\varepsilon_C)/2\), while transitions with \(J_{t+1}=J_t+1\) receive weight
\[
\alpha\,\mathbf 1\{U_{t+1}=U_t\}
\quad\text{when }A_t=1,
\qquad
\frac{\alpha}{2}
\quad\text{when }A_t=0,
\]
and all other hidden transitions receive weight zero.  The finite reward symbols are mapped to real rewards by \(0\mapsto -1\) and \(1\mapsto 1\), and the trajectory law is the finite chronological law generated by this initial distribution, behavior policy, and kernel, then embedded into the unrestricted real-reward raw experiment.

review.note: Unfolding signedDepthFinite and embed gives the stated constant observed state, packed depth-sign state, policies, reset/advance dynamics, conditionally independent signed reward emission, and behavior-stationary initialization on the stated positive-parameter domain.

nl.statement: Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}:=\sigma(A_1,Y_1,\ldots,A_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\), \(\ell_t:=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), \(q_t^v:=\Pr_v(J_t=Q\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\), and \(a_t^{(Q)}:=L^{-(Q-\ell_t)}\prod_{j=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}\mathbf 1\{A_j=1\}\), with an empty product equal to one.
nl.frozen_body:
Define
\[
\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}
:=
\sigma(A_0,Y_0,\ldots,A_{t-1},Y_{t-1}),
\]
\[
\ell_t:=\min\{Q,t\},
\]
\[
q_t^v
:=
\Pr_v(J_t=Q\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]

L^{-(Q-\ell_t)}

\]

nl.statement: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the following derivation handle: scale the reset-sign perturbation in \(\mathrm{def{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}family}\) to obey \(d_e/d_b\le1+\delta_T\), derive its observed-path testing modulus as a joint function of \(Q\) and \(\delta_T\), and pair that modulus with a data-dependent selector between immediate weighting and the partial-history scores \(Z_t(k)\). The output object is the sharp risk function \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)\), not a preassigned rate formula.
nl.frozen_body:
The derivation handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) consists of the following calculation: scale the reset-sign perturbation in the signed-depth construction so that
\[
\frac{d_e}{d_b}\le 1+\delta_T,
\]
derive the observed-path testing modulus as a joint function of \(Q\) and \(\delta_T\), and combine that modulus with a data-dependent selector between immediate weighting and the partial-history scores \(Z_t(k)\). Its output is the sharp risk function
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T).
\]

nl.statement: Let the state be \(s=(g,d_1,d_2,x_1,x_2,a_1)\) in \(\{50,100,150,200,250\}\times\{0,78\}^2\times\{0,31,850\}^2\times\{0,1\}\), giving \(360\) states. The diet coordinates \((d_1,d_2)\) form \(H_t\); all other coordinates form \(X_t\). Put \(b(1\mid X_t)=0.3\) and \(e(1\mid X_t)=\mathbf 1\{g\ge125\}\). With probability \(1/2\), draw the next full state uniformly. Otherwise draw \(d_0\in\{0,78\}\) with probabilities \((0.8,0.2)\), draw \(x_0\in\{0,31,850\}\) with probabilities \((0.4,0.4,0.2)\), draw \(\xi\sim N(0,25)\), set \(g'=\operatorname{round}_{\{50,100,150,200,250\}}\operatorname{clip}_{[50,250]}(10+0.9g+0.1d_1+0.1d_2-0.01x_1-0.01x_2-2A_t-4a_1+\xi)\), and shift the memories to \((g',d_0,d_1,x_0,x_1,A_t)\). Set \(Y_t=-1\) for \(g\le70\), \(Y_t=-2/3\) for \(g>150\), \(Y_t=-1/3\) for \(70<g\le80\) or \(120<g\le150\), and \(Y_t=0\) otherwise. This defines \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{grid}}\).

\quad\text{with probabilities}\quad

nl.statement: For every fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), and \(C\ge1\), there is \(c^\star<\infty\), independent of \(T\), \(|\mathcal X|\), and \(|\mathcal H|\), such that \(\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}E_M[(\widehat\theta_{k_T}-\theta(K,e))^2]\le c^\star T^{-\beta}\) for all sufficiently large \(T\). In particular, the overlapping-history covariance sum is geometric and introduces no logarithmic loss.
nl.frozen_body:
Fix constants satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Mixing scale.)} \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Policy-overlap scale.)} \(\zeta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-overlap radius.)} \(C\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(k_T\) be the balanced history depth in \cref{obj:def:history-depth}, and set
\[
\beta=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta}.
\]
Then there exist constants \(c^\star>0\) and \(T_\star\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_\star\), the estimator-specific worst-case squared risk from \cref{obj:synth_13} of the observable PHIW estimator \(\widehat\theta_{k_T}\) from \cref{obj:def:phiw-estimator} satisfies
\[
R_T(t_0,\zeta,C;\widehat\theta_{k_T})
\le
c^\star T^{-\beta}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(T\ge T_\star\), every finite alphabet sizes \(n_X,n_H\), and every raw POMDP experiment \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), the variance under the observed trajectory law induced by \(M\) of the unclipped partial-history average
\[
\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T)
\]
satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}
\!\left(\frac{1}{T-k_T}\sum_{t=k_T}^{T-1} Z_t(k_T)\right)
\le
\frac{2}{T}
\left[
e^{\zeta(k_T+1)}
\left(1+\frac{4}{e^\zeta-1}\right)
+
\frac{4}{1-e^{-1/t_0}}
\right].
\]

review.note: The quantifier order makes cStar uniform in T and both alphabet sizes, the worst-case squared-risk bound is eventual with exponent beta, and the additional variance inequality is the explicit geometric no-log covariance consequence.

nl.statement: For every fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C>1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth construction belongs to \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for every positive horizon \(T\). Its policy-induced stationary laws satisfy \(d_r(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_C r^j)/2\) when action one is taken with probability \(r\), \(\max_{j,u}d_e(j,u)/d_b(j,u)\le1+\varepsilon_C\le C\), and \(\theta(K,e)=vc_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q\).
nl.frozen_body:
For every \(T\ge 1\), \(Q\ge 1\), \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(C>1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let \(M_{Q,v}^T\) be the signed-depth experiment of \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family}.  Put
\[
\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\},
\qquad
L=\exp(\zeta),
\qquad
w_j=\frac{(1-\alpha(t_0))\alpha(t_0)^j}{1-\alpha(t_0)^{Q+1}},
\]
where \(\alpha(t_0)\) is the mixing factor and \(j=0,\ldots,Q\).  Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Membership.)} \(M_{Q,v}^T\in \mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Behavior stationary law.)} For every hidden state \(h\), with decoded depth \(j(h)\in\{0,\ldots,Q\}\) and sign \(u(h)\in\{-1,+1\}\),
\[
d_b(0,h)
=
w_{j(h)}
\frac{1+u(h)\varepsilon_C L^{-j(h)}}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Constant action-one stationary laws.)} For every \(r\in[0,1]\), if \(d_r\) denotes the stationary law induced by the constant policy that chooses action one with probability \(r\), then for every hidden state \(h\),
\[
d_r(0,h)
=
w_{j(h)}
\frac{1+u(h)\varepsilon_C r^{j(h)}}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target-over-behavior domination.)} For every joint state \(s\),
\[
d_e(s)\le (1+\varepsilon_C)d_b(s),
\qquad
1+\varepsilon_C\le C.
\]
\end{itemize}
The stationary target value of \cref{obj:def:target-value} is
\[
\theta(K,e)
=
v\,c_0(t_0)\,\varepsilon_C\,w_Q .
\]

review.note: Bool exactly encodes the two signs, the generic stationary-law identity covers every probability r, and its strictly positive behavior cells make the pointwise domination equivalent to the stated maximum density-ratio bound.

nl.statement: For the signed-depth alternatives, there exists \(B_0<\infty\), independent of \(Q\) and \(T\), such that \(\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})\le B_0T\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\). More precisely, for every observed history, \(E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]=vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v\) and \(q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q\) for a finite \(K_0\) depending only on \(t_0\), so the bound includes all stationary initial windows \(t\le Q\) without revealing reset times.
nl.frozen_body:
Fix \(t_0>0\), and write \(\alpha=\exp(-1/t_0)\). There exists a constant \(K_0>0\), depending on \(t_0\), such that whenever the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap exponent.)} \(\zeta>0\), and \(L=\exp(\zeta)\).
\item \textbf{(Reset amplitude.)} \(C>1\), and \(\varepsilon_C=\min\{(C-1)/2,1/2\}\).
\item \textbf{(Sequential ignorability.)} For every horizon \(T\), terminal depth \(Q\ge 1\), and alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth experiment in \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:sequential-ignorability}.
\item \textbf{(Stationary start.)} For every horizon \(T\), terminal depth \(Q\ge 1\), and alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the signed-depth experiment in \cref{obj:def:signed-depth-family} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start}.
\end{itemize}
there exists a constant \(B_0>0\), depending on \(t_0,\zeta,C\), such that for every \(T\) and every \(Q\ge 1\), with \(\mathbb P_{Q,v}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\) denoting the observed-path law of the signed-depth alternative \(v\),
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\middle\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\right)
\le
B_0\,T\,\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]
Moreover, for each \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), each \(t<T\), and each observed prefix \(o\in\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), the conditional reward mean satisfies the exact finite-prefix identity
\[
\mathbb E_v[Y_t\mid \mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}=o]
=
v\,c_0\,\varepsilon_C\,a_t^{(Q)}(o)\,q_t^v(o),
\]
where \(c_0=(1-\alpha)/4\), and \(a_t^{(Q)}\) and \(q_t^v\) are the rare-action-history factor and terminal-depth posterior from \cref{obj:def:filter-quantities}. The posterior satisfies
\[
q_t^v(o)\le K_0\,\alpha^Q .
\]
The same observed-path laws also satisfy
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\middle\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\right)
\le
\frac{4c_0^2K_0^2}{1-c_0^2}\,
T\,\varepsilon_C^2\,\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]

\le

\[

\le

Let \(T\ge1\), \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M_0,M_1\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} have the same observed-alphabet cardinality and the same behavior and target policies \(b\) and \(e\). Write \(\mathbb P_j\) for the observed-data law of \(M_j\) and \(\theta_j\) for its target value of \cref{obj:def:target-value}, \(j\in\{0,1\}\). Let \(s\ge0\) and \(\chi\ge0\), and assume
\[
2s\le|\theta_0-\theta_1|,\qquad
\mathbb P_0\ll\mathbb P_1,\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)\le\chi,\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)<\infty.
\]
Then the following hold. (i) For every raw estimator \(\widehat\theta\), a real-valued map of the observed-alphabet size, the policy pair, and the observed path that is measurable in the observed path for each alphabet size and policy pair, and whose squared errors \((\widehat\theta-\theta_j)^2\), evaluated at the alphabet size and policies of \(M_j\), are \(\mathbb P_j\)-integrable for \(j=0,1\),
\[
\frac{s^2e^{-\chi}}{4}\le\max\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{M_0}\bigl[(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)^2\bigr],\ \mathbb E_{M_1}\bigl[(\widehat\theta-\theta_1)^2\bigr]\Bigr\}.
\]
(ii) The minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\frac{s^2e^{-\chi}}{4}\le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C).
\]
Part (i) follows from Le Cam's two-point testing inequality \(\bigl(1-\mathrm{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\bigr)/2\le\max_j\mathbb P_j\{s\le|\widehat\theta-\theta_j|\}\), which uses the separation \(2s\le|\theta_0-\theta_1|\) and the common policies; the Bretagnolle--Huber inequality \(\frac12\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_0\|\mathbb P_1)\}\le1-\mathrm{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\) together with the KL bound; and Markov's inequality \(s^2\,\mathbb P_j\{s\le|\widehat\theta-\theta_j|\}\le\mathbb E_{M_j}[(\widehat\theta-\theta_j)^2]\). Part (ii) applies (i) to each bounded measurable observable-data estimator in the minimax infimum, whose squared errors are integrable, and bounds its supremum risk over the class below by its maximum risk over \(M_0\) and \(M_1\).

Let \(T\ge1\) and \(t_0,\zeta,C\in\mathbb R\), and let \(M=(\mathcal X,\mathcal H,K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T))\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. For a joint state \(s=(x,h)\) and an action \(a\in\{0,1\}\), write \(\bar r(s,a):=\int y\,K(dy,ds'\mid s,a)\) for the reward-coordinate mean of the kernel row \(K(\cdot\mid s,a)\); this row is a probability law for every \((s,a)\), including rows of zero realized probability, and the integral is read as \(0\) if the reward coordinate is not integrable, so \(\bar r(s,a)\) and \(g_e(s)=\sum_{a}e(a\mid x)\bar r(s,a)\) are defined everywhere. Then the target value of \cref{obj:def:target-value} satisfies
\[
\theta(K,e)=\sum_{s}d_e(s)g_e(s)\in[-1,1].
\]
Indeed, if \(d_b(s)>0\) and \(b(a\mid x)>0\), then \cref{obj:ass:stationary-start,obj:ass:sequential-ignorability} give the first-epoch event \(\{S_0=s,A_0=a\}\) positive probability, \cref{obj:ass:pomdp-kernel} identifies its conditional reward-successor law with \(K(\cdot\mid s,a)\), and \cref{obj:ass:bounded-reward} gives \(|\bar r(s,a)|\le1\). If \(d_e(s)>0\) and \(e(a\mid x)>0\), then \cref{obj:ass:latent-stationary-overlap} gives \(d_b(s)>0\) and \cref{obj:ass:policy-overlap} gives \(b(a\mid x)>0\), so \(|\bar r(s,a)|\le1\) on every such row. Actions with \(e(a\mid x)=0\) contribute \(0\) to \(g_e(s)\) whatever the value of \(\bar r(s,a)\), and \(e(\cdot\mid x)\) is a probability vector, so \(|g_e(s)|\le1\) whenever \(d_e(s)>0\); averaging against the probability vector \(d_e\) gives \(|\theta(K,e)|\le1\).
